inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 5,699.7M basic shares on issue at 2026-07-29 (10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~35M dilutive awards (H1-2026 weighted diluted 5,733M; FY2026 guidance assumes ~5.74B). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. No buybacks since FY2022 and none planned until de-levered, so the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge, not by repurchases.
inputs.cash_note: Cash 976 + short-term investments 10,723 at 2026-06-28 (10-Q balance sheet). Short-term investments are AFS/HTM government and corporate debt plus 1,630 of listed equities; treated as cash-like because they fund the interest income stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule). Long-term investments 1,559 carried separately in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, share-based compensation expense add-back ($799M; XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation). Pfizer does not separately disclose cash taxes paid on net-share settlement in XBRL or the cash flow statement, so no equity-award tax is added; at ~1.3% of revenue the omission is immaterial to value (<$0.10/share).
inputs.buyback_note: Zero repurchases FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and H1-2026 (cash flow statement). $3.3B authorisation remaining is unused; management states buybacks resume only after de-levering, and that leverage stays flat or modestly higher through the 2026-2030 LOE transition.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST, Oct-2026), ERP 4.5%, equity beta ~0.8 (defensive pharma lifted for the patent-cliff and US drug-pricing policy exposure) gives cost of equity ~7.8-8.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (A-rated curve), after-tax ~4.1%. Market-value weights ~72% equity (161B) / 28% debt (63B). WACC = 0.72 x 8.0 + 0.28 x 4.1 = ~6.9%, rounded to 7.0% and held identical across scenarios so risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not twice through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost ($498M FY2025) sits inside SI&A/COGS and therefore inside the EBITDA margin; operating lease liabilities (~$2.6B) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are small ($302M at 2026-06-28); flows are consolidated and NCI is deducted once in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: US operating company, large-cap pharma; not a bank/REIT/LIC). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue 62,579; year 1 of the path = FY2026, guided 60.5-62.5B). The FY2022 COVID peak (101B) and the 2023-25 unwind are excluded from every anchor: pre-COVID owner-FCF margins ran 23-31%, the FY2021-22 peak 25-35%, and FY2023-25 4-13% as Paxlovid/Comirnaty revenue, rebate accruals and the Paxlovid government credit unwound through working capital. Q2 2026 GAAP loss of $248M is a $3.8B IPR&D impairment (sigvotatug vedotin, failed Phase 3 SigVie-002, June 2026) plus $525M Oxbryta write-off and $419M restructuring; adjusted income was flat YoY at $4.44B, so the loss is one-off. NORMALISED EBITDA MARGIN: Pfizer's own adjusted EBITDA runs ~38% of revenue because it excludes acquired IPR&D (~$1.6B FY2025), restructuring (~$1.1B) and legal charges (~$1.0B). All three have recurred every year for a decade and in-licensing is how the pipeline is replenished, so the house margin treats them as operating costs: ~32.5% on FY2025. CASH TAX: adjusted ETR is guided ~15%, but ~$4.7B/yr of intangible amortisation from the Seagen stock deal is largely non-deductible (hence the ~$2.1B/yr deferred-tax benefit) and the final TCJA transition-tax instalment fell in 2025. The cash rate is modelled on EBIT after full book D&A at 26% in 2026 easing to 22% as the Wyeth/Hospira/Seagen amortisation schedule (4.7B 2026 -> 2.7B 2030) runs off; this reproduces ~$3.2-3.5B of cash tax on the guided adjusted base. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables+inventory exceed payables, so growth consumes cash and the LOE-driven revenue decline releases it; capture -8% on the revenue change. Net debt uses the 2026-06-28 balance sheet; interest income ($603M FY2025) is stripped because the $10.7B of short-term investments that earn it are netted against debt. YEAR-1 FCF vs FY2025: the component build gives ~13.0B unlevered owner FCF for FY2026 (21% of revenue) against 7.7B levered owner FCF in FY2025 (12%); the gap is interest paid (2.7B, excluded from an unlevered build discounted at WACC), the final ~1.2B TCJA transition-tax instalment, and ~2-3B of COVID-era working-capital unwind (rebate accruals, Paxlovid government credit) that does not recur.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term investments (equity securities, private equity, HTM debt) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: 10-Q 2026-06-28 balance sheet; not part of the interest-bearing pile netted in net_debt

equity_bridge.item: Contingent consideration: Metsera CVRs (632) + Zihipp milestones (643) at acquisition fair value
equity_bridge.note: 10-Q Note 2A; approximate, excludes smaller legacy CVRs; FV changes of +550 in H1-2026 suggest the true liability is somewhat higher

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case forward path: 10-year revenue CAGR FY2025-FY2035 of roughly -0.1% (LOE trough ~55B in 2029-30, recovery to ~62B by 2035). Every historical CAGR is discarded: 3-year windows start at the FY2022 COVID peak (101B revenue, 29.9B owner FCF) and 5-year windows start at the FY2020 pre-boom base, so they measure the Paxlovid/Comirnaty cycle, not the business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR +6.5% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR -3.7% and revenue +8.5%: divergence >30% on EPS. Equity grew on retained COVID-era earnings while EPS collapsed from $5.59 (FY2022) to $1.37 (FY2025) as that revenue unwound and $4.9B/yr of impairments hit. None of the three is a forward proxy.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2020 11,324; FY2021 28,633; FY2022 24,908; FY2023 2,644; FY2024 8,413; FY2025 7,673. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (-32.5%) is below reported (-29.6%) because interest income rose from 251 to 603 over the window while FCF fell; SBC itself was stable at 0.9-1.4% of revenue. Pre-COVID owner-FCF margins: FY2016 25.0%, FY2017 25.9%, FY2018 30.8%, FY2019 23.5%, FY2020 27.2%. FY2016-17 revenue in the CSV (52.8B / 52.5B) is pre-Upjohn-spin and pre-consumer-JV; FY2018-19 (40.8B / 40.9B) is restated continuing operations, so the 2016-2019 revenue series is not like-for-like.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the upper half of the 60.5-62.5B guidance (~62.0B; H1 was +4% reported, +2% operational, and Pfizer has beaten midpoint in each of the last three years). FY2027 -2.5%: Ibrance/Xtandi Medicare MFP prices take effect, Xeljanz and Prevnar 13 erosion, Comirnaty/Paxlovid keep fading, offset by Padcev (+23%), Vyndaqel, Nurtec, Abrysvo, Lorbrena. FY2028 -5.0%: Eliquis US generic entry (April 2028; ~7.5B global franchise for Pfizer) and Ibrance LOE. FY2029 -4.0%: Vyndaqel/Vyndamax US erosion, Xtandi LOE tail. Trough revenue ~55B in FY2029-30, consistent with management's 'significantly accelerating' LOE language (~1.1B drag in 2026, ~4.5B by 2027 per the Analysis JSON) and ~17-18B of cumulative at-risk revenue. FY2031-35 +2-2.5%: launched/acquired products (Padcev, Elrexfio, Hympavzi, atirmociclib, vepdegestrant, mevrometostat, PD-1xVEGF from 3SBio/Innovent) and a modest Metsera obesity contribution offset the remaining tail; no blockbuster obesity outcome is assumed in base.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 normalised ~32.5% (revenue 62,579 less COGS 16,067, SI&A 13,794, R&D 10,437, plus ~1.74B depreciation embedded in those lines = 24.0B adjusted EBITDA; less acquired IPR&D 1,613, restructuring 1,092, legal ~1,000 treated as recurring = 20.3B). 2026 32.0%: includes the ~$0.6B Innovent upfront charged in Q3-2026 and the final $600M of the 5.7B cost-realignment savings. 2027-29 compresses to 30.0% as fixed R&D (guided 10.5-11.5B) and SI&A fall slower than high-margin Eliquis/Ibrance alliance revenue, partly offset by the additional $2.5B of 2027-29 productivity savings (1.0B SI&A, ~1.5B manufacturing optimisation). Recovers to 31% from 2032 as launched products scale; never returns to Pfizer's 38% adjusted basis because BD, restructuring and legal stay in the cost base.
base.da_rationale: Book D&A 6,592 FY2025 (10.5%) = ~1.75B depreciation + ~4.85B intangible amortisation. Pfizer's own schedule: amortisation 4,677 (2026), 4,087 (2027), 3,723 (2028), 2,775 (2029), 2,732 (2030). Path is (schedule + ~1.75B depreciation) / projected revenue, with ~0.5B added from 2030 for Metsera IPR&D (7.9B) converting to amortising intangibles on approval, then declining to 6% as legacy Wyeth/Hospira/Seagen intangibles complete.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 2,629 (4.2%), FY2024 2,909 (4.6%), H1-2026 969 annualising ~3.2%. Set 4.3% then 4.5%: the Sept-2025 US onshoring/MFN agreement with the administration commits to additional US manufacturing capex and the Manufacturing Optimization Program is entering its next phase, so recent run-rate is a floor not a norm.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes 4,688 FY2025 included the final TCJA transition-tax instalment (~1.2B); normal ~3.5B. Guided adjusted ETR ~15% is on adjusted pre-tax (~20B) which excludes amortisation; because the Seagen amortisation is largely non-deductible, that 3.1-3.5B of cash tax is 26-28% of EBIT after full book D&A. Rate eases to 22% as the non-deductible amortisation runs off and EBIT rises toward the adjusted base. OBBBA lowers the GILTI/NCTI rate to 12.6% from 2026, so the ~15% adjusted ETR is durable; Pillar 2 is the upside risk to the rate.
base.terminal_rationale: Terminal growth 2.0%: mature pharma on a perpetual LOE treadmill grows slower than nominal GDP without M&A, and the house does not credit unannounced M&A. Cap 15x year-10 FCF (method: 12-15x for structurally slower businesses) is expected to bind over Gordon at 7%/2% (20.4x); the cap, not Gordon, sets the terminal value.

bull.narrative: Pipeline delivers on schedule: Metsera MET-097i monthly GLP-1 and the MET-097i+MET-233i combination read out positively in Phase 3 (2027-28) and launch into a $100B+ obesity market by 2029; PD-1xVEGF (SSGJ-707 via 3SBio) and Innovent assets reach the market 2029-30; atirmociclib, vepdegestrant and mevrometostat extend the breast/prostate franchises past the Ibrance/Xtandi LOEs; Padcev reaches $5B+. LOE drag is as scheduled but Eliquis ex-US erosion is slower and Vyndaqel holds share longer. The $6.7B cost programme plus manufacturing optimisation lifts margins to 34% by 2033 despite the revenue trough, and the Sept-2025 MFN agreement keeps US pricing and tariff policy predictable through the cliff. Revenue bottoms ~59B in 2029 and reaches ~72B by 2035 (3.6% 10-yr CAGR from FY2025, roughly consensus-bull).

bear.narrative: The cliff is steeper and the replacements fail: FY2026 lands at the guidance low end as Comirnaty/Paxlovid fade faster; Most-Favored-Nation pricing extends from the Medicaid/TrumpRx terms of the Sept-2025 agreement into Medicare and commercial channels, cutting US net price across Eliquis, Vyndaqel and Padcev; the three-year Section 232 tariff deferral in that agreement lapses or unravels into a 2028-29 tariff hit on imported product just as Eliquis and Ibrance generics arrive (2027-28) and Vyndaqel follows (2028-29). Metsera's monthly GLP-1 disappoints in Phase 3 (another sigvotatug), the PD-1xVEGF class does not displace Keytruda, and the $7.9B Metsera IPR&D is impaired. Revenue falls to ~49B by 2030 and grows only 1-1.5% thereafter; fixed R&D and SI&A on a smaller base push the normalised margin to 25.5-26% despite cost cuts. Leverage rises, the dividend is held but not grown, and legal/BD charges continue at ~2.5B/yr. Revenue 10-yr CAGR -2.7%.

scenario_narratives.base: Pfizer works through the 2026-2030 patent cliff as management describes it: ~$1.1B of LOE drag in 2026 accelerating sharply as Ibrance/Xtandi Medicare negotiated prices start in 2027, Eliquis US generics arrive in April 2028 and Vyndaqel erodes in 2028-29, taking revenue from ~62B to a ~55B trough in 2029-30. Launched and acquired products (growing 18% operationally in Q2-26: Padcev, Vyndaqel, Nurtec, Abrysvo, Lorbrena, Elrexfio, Hympavzi) and the first in-licensed/Metsera contributions bring revenue back to ~62B by 2035, but the house does not credit an obesity blockbuster or unannounced M&A. Normalised EBITDA margin compresses from 32% to 30% through the trough (fixed R&D of 10.5-11.5B against falling high-margin alliance revenue, partly offset by the $6.7B cost programme) and recovers to 31%. Acquired IPR&D, restructuring and legal costs (~3.5B/yr) are treated as recurring operating costs, which is why the house margin sits ~6pp below Pfizer's adjusted basis. The dividend (~9.9B) is roughly covered by levered FCF through the trough with no buybacks and flat leverage, exactly as guided.
scenario_narratives.bull: The pipeline converts: Metsera's monthly GLP-1 and amylin combination succeed in Phase 3 and launch in 2029, PD-1xVEGF and the next-generation oncology assets (atirmociclib, vepdegestrant, mevrometostat) backfill the Ibrance/Xtandi/Eliquis losses, Padcev passes $5B, and the LOE trough is shallower (~59B in 2029). Margins expand to 34% on productivity savings. Revenue reaches ~72B by 2035. This requires several independent clinical and regulatory outcomes to go right within three years of a $3.8B Phase 3 failure, so it is weighted below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: LOEs land as scheduled while policy and pipeline both go wrong: MFN pricing spreads beyond Medicaid, the Section 232 tariff deferral lapses into a 2028-29 cost hit, Metsera's obesity programme fails or is late, and PD-1xVEGF underwhelms. Revenue falls to ~49B by 2030 and barely grows after; the normalised margin drops to ~26%; the $7.9B Metsera IPR&D joins the $4.9B (FY2025) and $4.3B (Q2-26) of impairments. The dividend is maintained from a shrinking cash base with leverage drifting up. No solvency event: Pfizer still generates ~7-8B of unlevered FCF at the trough, so this is a value-destruction case, not a going-concern case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default because the downside is not speculative: the 2027-2029 LOE schedule (Ibrance, Xtandi, Eliquis, Vyndaqel) is contractual and management itself says the revenue reduction will 'significantly accelerate', while US drug-pricing policy (MFN, IRA negotiation, the tariff deferral's 2028 expiry) and a $3.8B Phase 3 failure in June 2026 are live. Bull cut to 20% because it requires the Metsera obesity programme, PD-1xVEGF and at least two late-stage oncology assets to all succeed inside the cliff window; Pfizer has impaired $9.2B of acquired R&D in the last 18 months. Base 50%: the trough-and-recover path is what both management guidance and consensus describe.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Pfizer is valued as a mature pharmaceutical owner-FCF stream through a known patent cliff, at a 7% USD WACC with a 15x terminal cap. The COVID boom and its unwind are excluded from every anchor. The house basis charges acquired IPR&D, restructuring and legal costs as recurring, charges SBC in the flows with a flat share count, strips interest income against a net-debt figure that nets the short-term investment pile, and models cash tax on EBIT after non-deductible Seagen amortisation. Terminal value is capped at 15x year-10 FCF because a buyer at exit faces the same LOE treadmill. No credit is given for unannounced M&A or for an obesity blockbuster outside the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Eliquis US generic entry April 2028 and Ibrance/Xtandi LOE 2027-28: ~13-14B of high-margin alliance/oncology revenue with the exact erosion curve uncertain
Vyndaqel/Vyndamax (~6B+) US exclusivity contested; erosion timing 2028-2029 swings the trough by several billion

US drug pricing: IRA negotiated prices (Eliquis 2026 at ~62% below list, Ibrance/Xtandi 2027), Most-Favored-Nation terms spreading beyond the Sept-2025 Medicaid/TrumpRx agreement, and Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs (up to 100%) once that agreement's three-year deferral lapses in 2028
Pipeline execution after the sigvotatug Phase 3 failure: Metsera obesity (7.9B IPR&D at risk), PD-1xVEGF (3SBio/Innovent), atirmociclib, vepdegestrant
Treatment of acquired IPR&D, restructuring and legal (~3.5B/yr) as recurring: moving them to one-offs lifts the normalised margin ~6pp and the base IV materially
Terminal cap 15x binds over Gordon; the valuation is sensitive to that choice and to the 7% WACC on a long-duration dividend stream
Net debt 51.5B against ~13B unlevered FCF: no refinancing risk at A-grade, but no capacity for a large acquisition without equity or dividend pressure
